The project at a glance

A football club wants to decide whom to recruit, how to handle fixture congestion and which players need load management. The five weekly tasks became the steps of one analytics chain, following the CRISP-DM cycle. Estimated effort: 168 hours.

"""
Week 1 - Data Preprocessing and Exploratory Data Analysis
YuvaIntern | Virtual Data Science with Python | Summer Training 2026
Author  : Arpit Vats

Project : Sports Analytics Capstone (Premier League-style player metrics)
Purpose : Generate a SYNTHETIC player dataset that contains deliberate data-quality
          problems, clean it with a documented pipeline, and explore it visually.

DATA NOTE: No real or scraped data is used. All records are generated with NumPy
(seed = 42), so every number printed by this script is reproducible.

Outputs : visual_1_missing_heatmap.png, visual_2_age_vs_value.png,
          visual_3_correlation_matrix.png
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (10, 6)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: GENERATE SYNTHETIC DATASET WITH DELIBERATE DATA-QUALITY ISSUES
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
np.random.seed(42)
n_records = 1000

# Injury_History is built from an OBJECT array so that np.nan stays a real missing
# value. (np.random.choice(['Yes', np.nan]) silently converts np.nan into the text
# 'nan', which pandas does not treat as missing, so fillna() would never fire.)
injury_choices = np.array(['Yes', np.nan], dtype=object)

data = {
    'Player_ID': [f"PL{1000 + i}" for i in range(n_records)],
    'Name': [f"Player_{i}" for i in range(n_records)],
    'Age': np.random.choice([22, 25, 28, 31, 34, np.nan], size=n_records,
                            p=[0.2, 0.3, 0.2, 0.15, 0.1, 0.05]),
    'Position': np.random.choice(['Forward', 'Midfielder', 'Defender', 'Goalkeeper'],
                                 size=n_records),
    'Matches_Played': np.random.randint(0, 38, size=n_records),
    'Goals': np.random.poisson(lam=4, size=n_records),
    'Assists': np.random.poisson(lam=3, size=n_records),
    'Market_Value_M': np.random.exponential(scale=15.0, size=n_records),
    'Injury_History': np.random.choice(injury_choices, size=n_records, p=[0.15, 0.85]),
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Inject intentional problems for the cleaning demonstration
df = pd.concat([df, df.iloc[:15]], ignore_index=True)           # 15 duplicate rows
df.loc[df['Market_Value_M'] > 60, 'Market_Value_M'] = np.nan    # extreme values -> missing

raw_df = df.copy()          # snapshot of the raw table (used for the Figure 1 heatmap)
raw_rows = len(raw_df)

print("--- RAW DATA INITIAL ASSESSMENT ---")
df.info()

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: DATA CLEANING PIPELINE
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Remove exact duplicates (same Player_ID)
duplicate_count = int(df.duplicated(subset=['Player_ID']).sum())
df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=['Player_ID'], keep='first')
unique_rows = len(df)

# Missing-value profile of the de-duplicated data (before imputation)
age_nulls = int(df['Age'].isnull().sum())
value_nulls = int(df['Market_Value_M'].isnull().sum())
injury_nulls = int(df['Injury_History'].isnull().sum())

# 2. Missing categorical data: a blank injury entry means "no recorded injury"
df['Injury_History'] = df['Injury_History'].fillna('No')

# 3. Missing market values: median of the player's own position (values are right-skewed)
df['Market_Value_M'] = df.groupby('Position')['Market_Value_M'].transform(
    lambda x: x.fillna(x.median()))

# 4. Missing ages: overall median, then cast to integer
df['Age'] = df['Age'].fillna(df['Age'].median()).astype(int)

# 5. Remove players with zero matches (avoids division by zero in per-match ratios)
zero_match_rows = int((df['Matches_Played'] == 0).sum())
df = df[df['Matches_Played'] > 0].copy()
clean_rows = len(df)

# Validation: the cleaned table must be complete and free of duplicates
assert df.isnull().sum().sum() == 0, "Missing values remain after cleaning"
assert not df['Player_ID'].duplicated().any(), "Duplicates remain after cleaning"

print("\n--- CLEANED DATA ASSESSMENT ---")
df.info()

print("\n--- CLEANING SUMMARY ---")
print(f"Raw rows                      : {raw_rows}")
print(f"Duplicate rows removed        : {duplicate_count}  -> {unique_rows} unique players")
print(f"Missing Age (unique rows)     : {age_nulls} ({age_nulls / unique_rows:.1%})")
print(f"Missing Market_Value_M        : {value_nulls}")
print(f"Missing Injury_History        : {injury_nulls} ({injury_nulls / unique_rows:.1%})")
print(f"Zero-match players removed    : {zero_match_rows}")
print(f"Clean rows for analysis       : {clean_rows}")
print("Injury_History after cleaning  :", df['Injury_History'].value_counts().to_dict())

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: EXPLORATORY ANALYSIS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
numerical_features = df[['Age', 'Matches_Played', 'Goals', 'Assists', 'Market_Value_M']]
correlation_matrix = numerical_features.corr()
corr_goals_value = correlation_matrix.loc['Goals', 'Market_Value_M']
corr_age_value = correlation_matrix.loc['Age', 'Market_Value_M']

print("\n--- CORRELATION MATRIX ---")
print(correlation_matrix.round(2))
print("\nMean market value (EUR m) by age:")
print(df.groupby('Age')['Market_Value_M'].mean().round(1).to_string())

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: VISUALISATION
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Figure 1: Missing-data heatmap of the RAW table (before cleaning)
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
sns.heatmap(raw_df.isnull(), cbar=False, cmap='viridis', yticklabels=False)
plt.title('Figure 1: Spatial Heatmap of Missing System Values (Pre-Clean)', fontsize=14, pad=15)
plt.ylabel('Row Index')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('visual_1_missing_heatmap.png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

# Figure 2: Age vs market value with a second-degree trend line
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='Age', y='Market_Value_M', hue='Position', alpha=0.6, palette='deep')
sns.regplot(data=df, x='Age', y='Market_Value_M', scatter=False, color='red', order=2,
            label='Valuation Curve')
plt.title('Figure 2: Non-Linear Regression of Player Market Value Against Age', fontsize=14, pad=15)
plt.xlabel('Player Age (Years)')
plt.ylabel('Market Value (€ Millions)')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('visual_2_age_vs_value.png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

# Figure 3: Pearson correlation matrix
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.heatmap(correlation_matrix, annot=True, cmap='coolwarm', fmt=".2f", linewidths=0.5)
plt.title('Figure 3: Pearson Correlation Matrix of On-Field Metrics', fontsize=14, pad=15)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('visual_3_correlation_matrix.png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

print("\nProcessing complete! Visualisations saved locally as PNG files.")

"""
Week 2 - Advanced Visual Storytelling for Recruitment Decisions
YuvaIntern | Virtual Data Science with Python | Summer Training 2026
Author  : Arpit Vats

Purpose : Engineer performance features and build five executive-style visualisations
          that help a club board question its recruitment assumptions.

DATA NOTE: The dataset is SYNTHETIC (NumPy, seed = 42); no real player records are used.

Outputs : story_1_joint_scarcity.png, story_2_violin_valuation.png,
          story_3_bubble_efficiency.png, story_4_facet_ecdf.png, story_5_dual_axis.png
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

sns.set_theme(style="white")
plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.labelsize': 12,
    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    'ytick.labelsize': 10,
    'figure.titlesize': 16,
})

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: GENERATE DATASET AND ENGINEER FEATURES
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
np.random.seed(42)
n_records = 1000

data = {
    'Player_ID': [f"PL{1000 + i}" for i in range(n_records)],
    'Name': [f"Player_{i}" for i in range(n_records)],
    'Age': np.random.choice([21, 23, 25, 27, 29, 31, 33], size=n_records,
                            p=[0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.2, 0.13, 0.08, 0.04]),
    'Position': np.random.choice(['Forward', 'Midfielder', 'Defender', 'Goalkeeper'],
                                 size=n_records, p=[0.3, 0.35, 0.25, 0.1]),
    'Matches_Played': np.random.randint(5, 38, size=n_records),
    'Goals': np.random.poisson(lam=5, size=n_records),
    'Assists': np.random.poisson(lam=4, size=n_records),
    'Market_Value_M': np.random.exponential(scale=14.0, size=n_records),
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

df['Goal_Contribution'] = df['Goals'] + df['Assists']
df['Efficiency_Per_Match'] = df['Goal_Contribution'] / df['Matches_Played']   # Matches_Played >= 5
# Three equal-sized market-value tiers
df['Tier'] = pd.qcut(df['Market_Value_M'], q=3, labels=['Value Asset', 'Core Roster', 'Marquee Elite'])

# Summary statistics quoted in the report
age_summary = (df.groupby('Age')
                 .agg(Mean_Efficiency=('Efficiency_Per_Match', 'mean'),
                      Players=('Player_ID', 'count'))
                 .reset_index())
share_high_eff = (df['Efficiency_Per_Match'] > 0.4).mean()
share_low_eff = (df['Efficiency_Per_Match'] < 0.3).mean()
median_matches_by_tier = df.groupby('Tier', observed=True)['Matches_Played'].median()

print("--- SUMMARY STATISTICS ---")
print(age_summary.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nShare of players above 0.4 contributions per match : {share_high_eff:.1%}")
print(f"Share of players below 0.3 contributions per match : {share_low_eff:.1%}")
print("\nMedian matches played by tier:")
print(median_matches_by_tier.to_string())

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: FIVE VISUALISATIONS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualisation 1: joint scatter with density contours (talent scarcity)
g = sns.jointplot(data=df, x='Age', y='Efficiency_Per_Match', hue='Position',
                  kind='scatter', alpha=0.5, palette='Set2', height=7)
g.plot_joint(sns.kdeplot, color="gray", alpha=0.3, zorder=0, levels=5)
g.fig.suptitle('Figure 1: The Scarcity Matrix - Production Efficiency vs. Age', y=1.03)
g.ax_joint.set_xlabel('Player Age')
g.ax_joint.set_ylabel('Contributions Per Match (Goals + Assists)')
plt.savefig('story_1_joint_scarcity.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# Visualisation 2: violin plot of market value by position and tier
plt.figure(figsize=(11, 6))
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='Position', y='Market_Value_M', hue='Tier',
               palette='muted', inner='quartile', split=False)
plt.title('Figure 2: Financial Risk and Market Valuation Distributions across Tiers', pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Playing Position')
plt.ylabel('Market Value (€ Millions)')
sns.despine(left=True, bottom=True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('story_2_violin_valuation.png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

# Visualisation 3: bubble chart for forwards (goals, assists, value, age)
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
forwards = df[df['Position'] == 'Forward']
bubble = plt.scatter(x=forwards['Goals'], y=forwards['Assists'],
                     s=forwards['Market_Value_M'] * 15, c=forwards['Age'],
                     cmap='coolwarm', alpha=0.6, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
cbar = plt.colorbar(bubble)
cbar.set_label('Player Age', rotation=270, labelpad=15)
plt.title('Figure 3: Identification Profile of Efficient Targets (Forwards Group)', pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Goals Scored')
plt.ylabel('Assists Provided')
plt.annotate('High Efficiency Target Zone\n(High Output / Low Value Bubble Size)',
             xy=(9, 8), xytext=(3, 9),
             arrowprops=dict(facecolor='black', shrink=0.05, width=1, headwidth=6))
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('story_3_bubble_efficiency.png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

# Visualisation 4: ECDF grid (reliability of match availability)
g = sns.FacetGrid(df, col="Position", hue="Tier", palette="viridis", height=4, aspect=1)
g.map(sns.ecdfplot, "Matches_Played", linewidth=2)
g.add_legend(title="Market Segment")
g.fig.suptitle('Figure 4: Reliability Profiles - Cumulative Probability of Player Match Experience', y=1.08)
g.set_axis_labels("Total Matches Featured", "Cumulative Sample Probability")
plt.savefig('story_4_facet_ecdf.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# Visualisation 5: dual-axis chart - mean efficiency (line) and talent pool size (bars)
# CORRECTION: the original script drew the line at numeric x = 21..33 while the bars sat at
# categorical positions 0..6 on the same shared axis, so the efficiency line fell outside the
# visible area. Both series now use the same positions (0..6) with age labels on the x-axis.
x_pos = np.arange(len(age_summary))
fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))
ax2 = ax1.twinx()

bars = ax2.bar(x_pos, age_summary['Players'], color='#e28743', alpha=0.3,
               label='Available Talent Pool (players)')
ax2.bar_label(bars, padding=2, fontsize=9, color='#a85a1f')
ax2.set_ylabel('Total Number of Available Players', color='#e28743')
ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#e28743')
ax2.set_ylim(0, age_summary['Players'].max() * 1.15)

ax1.plot(x_pos, age_summary['Mean_Efficiency'], color='#2b5c8f', marker='o', linewidth=3,
         label='Mean Efficiency (contributions per match)')
ax1.set_xticks(x_pos)
ax1.set_xticklabels(age_summary['Age'])
ax1.set_xlabel('Player Age')
ax1.set_ylabel('Mean Performance Efficiency', color='#2b5c8f')
ax1.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#2b5c8f')
ax1.set_ylim(age_summary['Mean_Efficiency'].min() - 0.05,
             age_summary['Mean_Efficiency'].max() + 0.05)
ax1.set_zorder(ax2.get_zorder() + 1)    # draw the line above the bars
ax1.patch.set_visible(False)

h1, l1 = ax1.get_legend_handles_labels()
h2, l2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax1.legend(h1 + h2, l1 + l2, loc='upper right')

plt.title('Figure 5: Executive Overview - Efficiency by Age vs. Talent Pool Size', pad=20)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('story_5_dual_axis.png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

print("\nExecution successful! All 5 storytelling visualisations saved as PNG files.")

"""
Week 3 - Hypothesis Testing on Fixture Congestion and Injury Risk
YuvaIntern | Virtual Data Science with Python | Summer Training 2026
Author  : Arpit Vats

Test 1  : Does attacking output fall when rest between matches is short?
            H0: mean goal contributions per 90 are equal (normal rest = congested rest)
            H1: mean under NORMAL rest (>= 4 days) is HIGHER than under CONGESTED rest (< 4 days)
Test 2  : Is high injury risk associated with playing position?
            H0: injury risk and position are independent
            H1: injury risk depends on position
Alpha   : 0.05

DATA NOTE: Both datasets are SYNTHETIC (NumPy, seed = 42). The congestion effect and the
position effect were built into the simulation, so these results demonstrate the testing
workflow rather than facts about real players.

Outputs : stat_1_density_distribution.png, stat_2_boxplot_intervals.png, stat_3_chi_heatmap.png
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.stats as stats
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (10, 6)
np.random.seed(42)

ALPHA = 0.05

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: GENERATE DATASETS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
n_samples = 500

# Group 1: normal rest (>= 4 days) - right-skewed output
normal_rest_output = np.random.gamma(shape=2.5, scale=0.25, size=n_samples)
# Group 2: congested rest (< 4 days) - slightly lower output simulated
congested_rest_output = np.random.gamma(shape=2.1, scale=0.25, size=n_samples)

df_stats = pd.DataFrame({
    'Rest_Condition': ['Normal Rest'] * n_samples + ['Congested Rest'] * n_samples,
    'Goal_Contributions_Per_90': np.concatenate([normal_rest_output, congested_rest_output]),
})

# Categorical data for the Chi-square test
positions = ['Forward', 'Midfielder', 'Defender']
injury_risk = ['Low Risk', 'High Risk']
df_chi = pd.DataFrame({
    'Position': np.random.choice(positions, size=600, p=[0.35, 0.40, 0.25]),
    'Injury_Status': np.random.choice(injury_risk, size=600, p=[0.70, 0.30]),
})
# Built-in dependency: forwards carry extra fatigue risk
df_chi.loc[(df_chi['Position'] == 'Forward') & (np.random.rand(len(df_chi)) > 0.4),
           'Injury_Status'] = 'High Risk'

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: STATISTICAL TESTING PIPELINE
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A. Normality (Shapiro-Wilk) for each group
stat_norm_a, p_norm_a = stats.shapiro(normal_rest_output)
stat_norm_b, p_norm_b = stats.shapiro(congested_rest_output)

# B. Equality of variances (Levene)
stat_lev, p_lev = stats.levene(normal_rest_output, congested_rest_output)

# C. Welch's t-test (does not assume equal variances).
#    CORRECTION: the original script reported only the default TWO-sided p-value although H1
#    is one-sided (normal > congested). Both versions are reported here.
t_stat, t_pval = stats.ttest_ind(normal_rest_output, congested_rest_output, equal_var=False)
_, t_pval_one = stats.ttest_ind(normal_rest_output, congested_rest_output, equal_var=False,
                                alternative='greater')

# Effect size (Cohen's d with pooled standard deviation)
pooled_sd = np.sqrt((normal_rest_output.var(ddof=1) + congested_rest_output.var(ddof=1)) / 2)
cohens_d = (normal_rest_output.mean() - congested_rest_output.mean()) / pooled_sd

# D. Mann-Whitney U (non-parametric; the data are right-skewed). One-sided: normal > congested
u_stat, u_pval = stats.mannwhitneyu(normal_rest_output, congested_rest_output, alternative='greater')

# E. Chi-square test of independence (position vs injury risk)
contingency_table = pd.crosstab(df_chi['Position'], df_chi['Injury_Status'])
chi2_stat, chi2_pval, dof, expected = stats.chi2_contingency(contingency_table)
cramers_v = np.sqrt(chi2_stat / (contingency_table.values.sum() * (min(contingency_table.shape) - 1)))
high_risk_share = contingency_table['High Risk'] / contingency_table.sum(axis=1)

def decision(p):
    return "Reject H0" if p < ALPHA else "Fail to reject H0"

print("--- STATISTICAL EXECUTION RESULTS (alpha = 0.05) ---")
print(f"Mean goal contributions per 90 : normal rest = {normal_rest_output.mean():.3f}, "
      f"congested rest = {congested_rest_output.mean():.3f}")
print(f"Shapiro-Wilk  : normal W={stat_norm_a:.3f}, p={p_norm_a:.2e} | "
      f"congested W={stat_norm_b:.3f}, p={p_norm_b:.2e}  -> data are not normal")
print(f"Levene        : F={stat_lev:.3f}, p={p_lev:.4f}  -> equal variances retained")
print(f"Welch t-test  : t={t_stat:.3f}, p(two-sided)={t_pval:.4f}, "
      f"p(one-sided)={t_pval_one:.4f}  -> {decision(t_pval_one)}")
print(f"Cohen's d     : {cohens_d:.3f} (small effect)")
print(f"Mann-Whitney U: U={u_stat:,.0f}, p(one-sided)={u_pval:.4f}  -> {decision(u_pval)}")
print(f"Chi-square    : chi2={chi2_stat:.2f}, dof={dof}, p={chi2_pval:.2e}, "
      f"Cramer's V={cramers_v:.3f}  -> {decision(chi2_pval)}")
print(f"Smallest expected count in Chi-square table: {expected.min():.1f} (rule of thumb: >= 5)")
print("\nObserved counts:")
print(contingency_table)
print("\nHigh-risk share by position:")
print(high_risk_share.round(3).to_string())

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: VISUALISATION
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Figure 1: density plot with group means
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.kdeplot(data=df_stats, x='Goal_Contributions_Per_90', hue='Rest_Condition', fill=True,
            common_norm=False, palette='Set1', alpha=0.4)
plt.axvline(normal_rest_output.mean(), color='blue', linestyle='--',
            label=f'Normal Mean ({normal_rest_output.mean():.2f})')
plt.axvline(congested_rest_output.mean(), color='red', linestyle='--',
            label=f'Congested Mean ({congested_rest_output.mean():.2f})')
plt.title('Figure 1: Performance Density Distribution Across Rest Conditions', pad=15)
plt.xlabel('Goal Contributions Per 90 Minutes')
plt.ylabel('Probability Density')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('stat_1_density_distribution.png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

# Figure 2: boxplot comparison (white dot = group mean)
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.boxplot(data=df_stats, x='Rest_Condition', y='Goal_Contributions_Per_90',
            hue='Rest_Condition', legend=False, palette='Set2', showmeans=True,
            meanprops={"marker": "o", "markerfacecolor": "white", "markeredgecolor": "black"})
plt.title('Figure 2: Performance Variance & Central Tendency Comparison', pad=15)
plt.xlabel('Rest Schedule Condition')
plt.ylabel('Goal Contributions Per 90 Minutes')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('stat_2_boxplot_intervals.png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

# Figure 3: Chi-square contingency heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
sns.heatmap(contingency_table, annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='YlGnBu', cbar=False)
plt.title('Figure 3: Observed Injury Risk Contingency Matrix Across Positions', pad=15)
plt.xlabel('Injury Risk Classification')
plt.ylabel('Playing Position')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('stat_3_chi_heatmap.png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

print("\nVisualisation generation complete! PNG files saved locally.")

"""
Week 4 - Injury-Risk Prediction with Machine Learning
YuvaIntern | Virtual Data Science with Python | Summer Training 2026
Author  : Arpit Vats

Purpose : Predict whether an athlete is at high (1) or low (0) risk of a soft-tissue injury
          in the next match micro-cycle, and compare two classifiers:
            - Logistic Regression (baseline, features standardised)
            - Random Forest (100 trees, max depth 5, untuned)

DATA NOTE: The dataset is SYNTHETIC (NumPy, seed = 42). The risk label is generated from a
logistic formula of workload, sleep and soreness, so the models are learning a known rule.

Outputs : ml_1_confusion_matrices.png, ml_2_roc_curves.png
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import (confusion_matrix, classification_report, roc_curve, auc,
                             accuracy_score, precision_score, recall_score, f1_score)

sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (10, 6)
np.random.seed(42)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: GENERATE SYNTHETIC ATHLETE WORKLOAD DATASET
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
n_samples = 1200

age = np.random.randint(18, 36, size=n_samples)
acwr = np.random.normal(loc=1.1, scale=0.3, size=n_samples)         # Acute:Chronic Workload Ratio
load_28d = np.random.normal(loc=120, scale=25, size=n_samples)      # 28-day load (not used in the label)
sleep = np.random.randint(3, 10, size=n_samples)
soreness = np.random.randint(1, 10, size=n_samples)

# Linear logit plus noise; the flag is 1 when the resulting probability exceeds 0.5
logit = (-3.5 + (1.8 * acwr) + (0.03 * age) + (0.35 * soreness) - (0.4 * sleep)
         + np.random.normal(0, 0.8, n_samples))
prob = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-logit))
injury_flag = (prob > 0.5).astype(int)

df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Age': age,
    'ACWR': acwr,
    'Cumulative_28Day_Load': load_28d,
    'Sleep_Quality': sleep,
    'Soreness_Score': soreness,
    'Injury_Risk_Flag': injury_flag,
})

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: PREPROCESSING AND MODEL TRAINING
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
X = df.drop('Injury_Risk_Flag', axis=1)
y = df['Injury_Risk_Flag']

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=42, stratify=y)

scaler = StandardScaler()
X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)      # fit on training data only
X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)

# Model 1: Logistic Regression
lr_model = LogisticRegression(random_state=42)
lr_model.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train)
y_pred_lr = lr_model.predict(X_test_scaled)
y_prob_lr = lr_model.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)[:, 1]

# Model 2: Random Forest (trees do not need scaling)
rf_model = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, max_depth=5, random_state=42)
rf_model.fit(X_train, y_train)
y_pred_rf = rf_model.predict(X_test)
y_prob_rf = rf_model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: EVALUATION (every metric quoted in the report is printed here)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
fpr_lr, tpr_lr, _ = roc_curve(y_test, y_prob_lr)
fpr_rf, tpr_rf, _ = roc_curve(y_test, y_prob_rf)
auc_lr = auc(fpr_lr, tpr_lr)
auc_rf = auc(fpr_rf, tpr_rf)

cm_lr = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred_lr)
cm_rf = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred_rf)

results = {}
for name, y_pred, cm, model_auc in [('Logistic Regression', y_pred_lr, cm_lr, auc_lr),
                                    ('Random Forest', y_pred_rf, cm_rf, auc_rf)]:
    tn, fp, fn, tp = cm.ravel()
    results[name] = {
        'Accuracy': accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred),
        'Precision': precision_score(y_test, y_pred),
        'Recall': recall_score(y_test, y_pred),
        'F1': f1_score(y_test, y_pred),
        'ROC-AUC': model_auc,
        'TN': tn, 'FP': fp, 'FN': fn, 'TP': tp,
    }

print("--- DATASET AND SPLIT ---")
print(f"Records: {len(df)} | train: {len(X_train)} | test: {len(X_test)}")
print(f"High-risk share (all data): {y.mean():.1%} | high-risk cases in test set: {int(y_test.sum())}")

print("\n--- MODEL COMPARISON (test set) ---")
print(pd.DataFrame(results).T.round(3).to_string())
for name, y_pred in [('Logistic Regression', y_pred_lr), ('Random Forest', y_pred_rf)]:
    print(f"\n{name} - classification report")
    print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred, target_names=['Low risk', 'High risk']))

print("--- FEATURE INFLUENCE ---")
print("Logistic Regression coefficients (standardised features):")
print(pd.Series(lr_model.coef_[0], index=X.columns).round(2).sort_values(ascending=False).to_string())
print("\nRandom Forest feature importances:")
print(pd.Series(rf_model.feature_importances_, index=X.columns).round(3).sort_values(ascending=False).to_string())

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: VISUALISATION
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Figure 1: side-by-side confusion matrices
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5))
sns.heatmap(cm_lr, annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='Blues', ax=axes[0], cbar=False)
axes[0].set_title('Logistic Regression Confusion Matrix')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Predicted Label')
axes[0].set_ylabel('True Label')
sns.heatmap(cm_rf, annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='Greens', ax=axes[1], cbar=False)
axes[1].set_title('Random Forest Confusion Matrix')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Predicted Label')
axes[1].set_ylabel('True Label')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('ml_1_confusion_matrices.png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

# Figure 2: ROC curve comparison
plt.figure(figsize=(9, 6))
plt.plot(fpr_lr, tpr_lr, color='blue', lw=2, label=f'Logistic Regression (AUC = {auc_lr:.3f})')
plt.plot(fpr_rf, tpr_rf, color='green', lw=2, label=f'Random Forest (AUC = {auc_rf:.3f})')
plt.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], color='gray', linestyle='--')
plt.title('Figure 2: Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Comparison', pad=15)
plt.xlabel('False Positive Rate (1 - Specificity)')
plt.ylabel('True Positive Rate (Recall)')
plt.legend(loc='lower right')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('ml_2_roc_curves.png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

print("\nModel pipeline execution complete! PNG charts saved locally.")

"""
Week 5 - Integrated Analytics Pipeline and Executive Summary
YuvaIntern | Virtual Data Science with Python | Summer Training 2026
Author  : Arpit Vats

Purpose : Run Weeks 1-4 as one end-to-end pipeline (clean -> explore -> visualise -> test ->
          predict), collect their headline results into a single summary table, and produce an
          executive dashboard. Nothing is re-implemented here, so the numbers always match the
          weekly scripts.

HOW TO RUN: keep the five week*.py files in the same folder and run this script. The weekly
scripts' own printouts are suppressed; only the consolidated summary is shown.

DATA NOTE: All data are SYNTHETIC (NumPy, seed = 42), so the findings demonstrate the method,
not facts about real football players.

Output  : week5_executive_dashboard.png (the weekly PNG figures are regenerated as well)
"""

import io
import runpy
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

try:
    BASE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
except NameError:               # running inside Jupyter / Colab
    BASE = Path.cwd()


def run_phase(filename):
    """Execute one weekly script silently and return its variables."""
    with redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
        return runpy.run_path(str(BASE / filename))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: RUN THE FOUR ANALYSIS PHASES
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
w1 = run_phase('week1_data_preprocessing.py')
w2 = run_phase('week2_visual_storytelling.py')
w3 = run_phase('week3_hypothesis_testing.py')
w4 = run_phase('week4_injury_risk_ml.py')

lr = w4['results']['Logistic Regression']
rf = w4['results']['Random Forest']

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: CONSOLIDATED RESULTS TABLE
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
summary = pd.DataFrame([
    ('1. Preprocessing', 'Rows: raw -> unique -> clean',
     f"{w1['raw_rows']} -> {w1['unique_rows']} -> {w1['clean_rows']}"),
    ('1. Preprocessing', 'Duplicates / zero-match rows removed',
     f"{w1['duplicate_count']} / {w1['zero_match_rows']}"),
    ('1. Preprocessing', 'Correlation of goals / age with market value',
     f"{w1['corr_goals_value']:.2f} / {w1['corr_age_value']:.2f}"),
    ('2. Visual storytelling', 'Mean efficiency range across age groups',
     f"{w2['age_summary']['Mean_Efficiency'].min():.2f} - {w2['age_summary']['Mean_Efficiency'].max():.2f}"),
    ('2. Visual storytelling', 'Players aged 29 / 31 / 33',
     " / ".join(str(int(n)) for n in w2['age_summary'].loc[w2['age_summary']['Age'] >= 29, 'Players'])),
    ('3. Hypothesis testing', 'Goal contributions per 90: normal vs congested rest',
     f"{w3['normal_rest_output'].mean():.2f} vs {w3['congested_rest_output'].mean():.2f}"),
    ('3. Hypothesis testing', 'Welch t-test (one-sided) / Mann-Whitney p-values',
     f"{w3['t_pval_one']:.4f} / {w3['u_pval']:.4f}"),
    ('3. Hypothesis testing', 'Chi-square (position vs injury risk)',
     f"chi2 = {w3['chi2_stat']:.2f}, p < 0.0001, V = {w3['cramers_v']:.2f}"),
    ('4. Machine learning', 'Logistic Regression: AUC / recall / precision',
     f"{lr['ROC-AUC']:.3f} / {lr['Recall']:.1%} / {lr['Precision']:.1%}"),
    ('4. Machine learning', 'Random Forest: AUC / recall / precision',
     f"{rf['ROC-AUC']:.3f} / {rf['Recall']:.1%} / {rf['Precision']:.1%}"),
], columns=['Phase', 'Metric', 'Result'])

print("=" * 78)
print("CONSOLIDATED RESULTS - SPORTS ANALYTICS CAPSTONE")
print("=" * 78)
print(summary.to_string(index=False))

print("\nRECOMMENDATIONS (to be validated on real club data before use)")
print("1. Rotation protocol: limit forwards' minutes in congested fixture spells "
      f"(high-risk share: forwards {w3['high_risk_share']['Forward']:.0%}, "
      f"midfielders {w3['high_risk_share']['Midfielder']:.0%}, defenders {w3['high_risk_share']['Defender']:.0%}).")
print("2. Load management: use the Logistic Regression model as a daily screening tool and "
      "tune the decision threshold to raise recall.")
print("3. Evidence before spending: market value showed no age or goal-count pattern, so rely on "
      "validated efficiency metrics rather than age or raw totals.")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: EXECUTIVE DASHBOARD (2 x 2)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 9))

# Panel A: data funnel
ax = axes[0, 0]
stages = ['Raw rows', 'After de-duplication', 'After cleaning']
counts = [w1['raw_rows'], w1['unique_rows'], w1['clean_rows']]
bars = ax.bar(stages, counts, color=['#9aa5b1', '#6c8ebf', '#2b5c8f'])
ax.bar_label(bars, padding=3)
ax.set_ylim(0, max(counts) * 1.12)
ax.set_title('A. Data preparation funnel (Week 1)')
ax.set_ylabel('Number of player records')

# Panel B: efficiency by age
ax = axes[0, 1]
age_summary = w2['age_summary']
x_pos = np.arange(len(age_summary))
ax.plot(x_pos, age_summary['Mean_Efficiency'], marker='o', linewidth=3, color='#2b5c8f')
ax.set_xticks(x_pos)
ax.set_xticklabels(age_summary['Age'])
ax.set_ylim(0.4, 0.75)
ax.set_xlabel('Player age')
ax.set_ylabel('Mean contributions per match')
ax.set_title('B. Efficiency by age group (Week 2)')

# Panel C: high-risk share by position
ax = axes[1, 0]
share = w3['high_risk_share'].sort_values(ascending=False)
bars = ax.bar(share.index, share.values * 100, color=['#c0504d', '#e28743', '#9aa5b1'])
ax.bar_label(bars, labels=[f"{v:.0%}" for v in share.values], padding=3)
ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
ax.set_ylabel('High-risk players (%)')
ax.set_title(f"C. Injury risk by position (Week 3, chi2 = {w3['chi2_stat']:.1f})")

# Panel D: ROC curves
ax = axes[1, 1]
ax.plot(w4['fpr_lr'], w4['tpr_lr'], color='blue', lw=2, label=f"Logistic Regression (AUC = {lr['ROC-AUC']:.3f})")
ax.plot(w4['fpr_rf'], w4['tpr_rf'], color='green', lw=2, label=f"Random Forest (AUC = {rf['ROC-AUC']:.3f})")
ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], color='gray', linestyle='--')
ax.set_xlabel('False positive rate')
ax.set_ylabel('True positive rate')
ax.set_title('D. Injury-risk models (Week 4)')
ax.legend(loc='lower right')

fig.suptitle('Sports Analytics Capstone - Executive Dashboard (synthetic data)', fontsize=16)
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])
fig.savefig('week5_executive_dashboard.png', dpi=300)
plt.close(fig)

print("\nPipeline complete! Dashboard saved as week5_executive_dashboard.png")

Limits and next steps

  • Every dataset is simulated, so the results show the method, not real football.
  • The congestion and position effects were built into the data, so significance was expected.
  • At the 50% cut-off the model misses about 41% of high-risk players, and the Random Forest was left untuned.
  • Next: repeat the pipeline on a real public dataset, tune the cut-off for recall, and add SHAP explanations.
